plan.title: bug(hooks): session hook rewrites the tracked AGENTS.md managed section from the pinned runtime in this repo, rolling it back

narratives.Description: In the framework source repository, `session:start`, `agents:refresh` and the self-complete setup that every hook call runs all plan the `AGENTS.md` managed section against the pinned runtime's copy of `agents-entry.md`, which is often older than the repository's own `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. A fresh worktree therefore gets its tracked section rolled back, and `agents:refresh` then reports the older section as current. This story makes the refresh plan read the checkout's own template file in a source checkout when the caller gives no template, and makes the setup writer stop passing the runtime template in a source checkout; consumer projects keep today's behaviour.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker in a worktree of the framework source repository, I want the session and setup steps to leave the tracked `AGENTS.md` alone when it matches the repository's own template, so that I do not restore it again and again or roll the managed rules back by committing it.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6507). 1. `packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts`: in `agentsRefreshPlan`, when no `frameworkRoot` and no `readTemplate` seam is given, `DEFT_ROOT` is unset and `isFrameworkSourceCheckoutAt(projectRoot)` is true, read `<projectRoot>/content/templates/agents-entry.md` directly and use `projectRoot` as the framework root (so the marker sha comes from the checkout). 2. `packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts`: in `ensureAgentsManagedSection`, skip the runtime template seams in a source checkout. 3. Tests: a new `packages/core/src/platform/agents-md-source-checkout-6507.test.ts` (current / stale / staged content package / consumer / explicit seams and `DEFT_ROOT`, with a walk template that differs from the fixture template); `packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring-framework-source.test.ts` (setup leaves a matching section alone while the runtime template differs; consumer still gets the runtime template); `packages/runtime/src/agents-refresh.test.ts` (no sha-match line on a stale source fixture). 4. One `changelog.d/` fragment that says the fix acts in this repository once a release carrying it is pinned.
narratives.Overview:
1. Plan. In `agentsRefreshPlan` (`packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts`), when the caller passes no `frameworkRoot` and no `readTemplate` seam, `DEFT_ROOT` is unset, and `isFrameworkSourceCheckoutAt(projectRoot)` is true, the plan reads the template from the file `<projectRoot>/content/templates/agents-entry.md` directly (not through `contentRoot`), and uses `projectRoot` as the framework root, so the marker sha of any write comes from the checkout.
2. Setup. In `ensureAgentsManagedSection` (`packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts`), when `isFrameworkSourceCheckoutAt(projectRoot)` is true, the call passes no `frameworkRoot` or `readTemplate` seam, so it takes item 1. Outside a source checkout it keeps passing the runtime package's template as today.
3. Unchanged. States, the `current` comparison, the writer, the lock and the CLI text stay as they are. Callers that pass their own seams (the health gate, `migrate:xbrief`, init) and an explicit `DEFT_ROOT` keep winning. In a consumer project both conditions are false, so the plan and the setup write are the same as today.
4. Pin timing. The fix acts in this repository when a release that carries it is pinned; the docs or changelog line says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a source-checkout fixture whose `AGENTS.md` managed section matches its own `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, and a different template on the module walk, when `applyAgentsRefresh` runs with no seams, then the state is `current` and `AGENTS.md` is not written.
- Given the same fixture, and a runtime template (the file `resolveRuntimeAgentsEntryTemplatePath()` returns, replaced in the test) whose rendered section differs from the fixture section, when `ensureAgentsManagedSection` runs, then `AGENTS.md` is not modified. A build that still passes the runtime template as `readTemplate` in a source checkout fails this criterion.
- Given a source-checkout fixture whose own template is newer than its `AGENTS.md` section, when `agentsRefreshPlan` runs with no seams, then the state is `stale`, the new content carries the checkout template, and the `agents:refresh` CLI does not print `unchanged - sha match`.
- Given a source-checkout fixture with a staged content package whose template differs, when `agentsRefreshPlan` runs with no seams, then it reads the checkout's `content/templates/agents-entry.md`.
- Given a consumer fixture (not a source checkout), when `agentsRefreshPlan` and `ensureAgentsManagedSection` run, then they use the same template as today.
- Given a source checkout with `DEFT_ROOT` set or an explicit `frameworkRoot` or `readTemplate` seam, when `agentsRefreshPlan` runs, then it uses that root or seam as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- A guard only inside `ensureAgentsManagedSection`: it leaves `session:start` orientation and `agents:refresh` on the runtime template (comment 6940422195, finding 1, road not taken).
- Ignoring every `readTemplate` seam in a source checkout: it would drop the health gate's committed-template read (comment 6940422195, finding 1).
- Reading the template through `contentRoot`: a staged content package can win over the checkout file (comment 6940422195, finding 2).
- A change that acts before the next pin: no code the current pin runs reads anything the source can change (comment 6940422195, answer 3).

## In plain English
This repository is the framework source. Its `AGENTS.md` managed section is generated from the repository's own template, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. But `session:start` and `deft agents:refresh` run the pinned runtime from `node_modules`, and that code reads the template shipped inside the pinned runtime, which is often older. So in a fresh worktree the session rewrites `AGENTS.md` back to the older text (it drops the #6379 line today), and `agents:refresh` then says the older text is current. Workers must restore the file each time and keep it out of every commit.

The recommended fix is one rule in the one function that plans every refresh: in a checkout of the framework source repository, read the template from that checkout, not from the runtime. Consumer projects are not source checkouts, so nothing changes for them. The questions for the critic are whether that one place covers every path that writes or judges the section, and whether the fix acting only after the next pin is acceptable.

## Pains
- P1 — When a session starts in a worktree of the framework source repository, the session rewrites the tracked `AGENTS.md` managed section from the pinned runtime's template (issue Acceptance Criterion 1).
- P2 — When the pinned runtime's template is older than the repository's source template, `agents:refresh` reports the older section as current ("unchanged - sha match") (Acceptance Criterion 2).
- P3 — Consumer projects need today's managed-section refresh unchanged; a fix for P1 and P2 that alters it would break every consumer (Acceptance Criterion 3).

## Constraints (not pains)
- No new gate, grant, refusal, flag or stored state.
- Out of scope (operator-confirmed deferral, chat 2026-11-17): any other consumer-style deposit written into the source repository beyond `AGENTS.md`. That goes to a follow-up issue.
- Do not overlap running stories: #6480 (`hooks/scope.ts`, `hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `scope/lands-with-product.ts`, `policy/write-fence.ts`) and #6296 (release tooling).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts` 33-70: `frameworkRoot(seams)` is the seam, else `DEFT_ROOT`, else a walk up from the module file; the template is `contentRoot(frameworkRoot)/templates/agents-entry.md`. Run from `node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime`, the walk stops at the runtime's own `templates/agents-entry.md`.
- `agents-md.ts` 335-492 `agentsRefreshPlan`: 469-477 returns `current` when the existing section, attributes stripped, equals the rendered template; else `stale` with the template text as new content. 525-554 `applyAgentsRefresh` writes `stale`, `missing` and `absent`.
- `packages/core/src/session/orientation-compression.ts` 354-367 and 547-555: the session-start orientation calls `applyAgentsRefresh(projectRoot, {})` with no seams; `session-start.ts` 2785-2787 passes a `frameworkRoot` option to orientation that this section does not use.
- `packages/runtime/src/agents-refresh.ts` 58-72: the CLI calls the same function and prints `unchanged - sha match` when the state is `current`.
- `packages/core/src/doctor/paths.ts` 45-62 `isFrameworkSourceCheckoutAt` (#6337): `main.md` plus the `DEFT_REPO_POSITIVE_MARKERS` files; linked worktrees answer true. 73-90 `resolveFrameworkRootForProject`: explicit root, then `DEFT_ROOT`, then the source checkout itself.
- `packages/core/src/eval/health.ts` 155-200: the `agents-md-freshness` gate already plans with `frameworkRoot: projectRoot` in the framework source (#5802).
- `packages/core/src/content-root.ts` 111-136: in a source checkout, in-repo `content/` wins over a hoisted runtime (#5802).
- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` 946-952: the #6337 guard for `.gitattributes` uses the same predicate.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts` 276-292: install passes the runtime's template to `applyAgentsRefresh` as an explicit seam.
- `AGENTS.md` 173 on master: marker `sha=4288b3cc02e1`, a git sha, so the committed section was refreshed with the source checkout as framework root.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1. In `agentsRefreshPlan`, when the caller passes no `frameworkRoot` and no `readTemplate` seam, `DEFT_ROOT` is unset, and `isFrameworkSourceCheckoutAt(projectRoot)` is true, the plan uses `projectRoot` as the framework root. The template is then the checkout's own `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. This is the order `resolveFrameworkRootForProject` already uses.
- R2. Nothing else changes: the same states, the same `current` comparison, the same writer. In a worktree whose `AGENTS.md` matches its own template the state is `current` and nothing is written. When the checkout's template is newer than its `AGENTS.md`, the refresh writes the newer section (today's #1309 propagation).
- R3. In a consumer project the predicate is false, so the plan is byte-for-byte today's.
- R4. Tests: a temporary source-checkout fixture whose template differs from the template the module walk finds gives `current` when its `AGENTS.md` matches its own template, and `stale` (with its own template as new content) when it does not; a consumer fixture keeps today's template source; explicit seams and `DEFT_ROOT` still win.
- R5. The session hook and `deft agents:refresh` run the pinned runtime's code, so in this repository the fix takes effect when a release that carries it is pinned. Until then the drift clears at each pin, as the issue notes.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is `agentsRefreshPlan` the right single place, or does another path in the source repository write or judge the managed section from the runtime template (doctor, host-content surface, migrate, install)?
2. Should explicit seams and `DEFT_ROOT` keep winning in the source checkout, given that install passes the runtime template explicitly (`setup-wiring.ts` 276-292)?
3. Is R5 acceptable for Acceptance Criterion 1, or is a change needed that acts before the next pin?

Read from the dest checkout whose HEAD file is 139fdc3bb87b2a2bc2bf7382cb0caffc0166f6ee. The shell hook refused git show because `node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime` is absent.

## In plain English

This repository's tracked `AGENTS.md` managed section is generated from `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. In a fresh worktree the running code is the pinned runtime, and that copy of the template is older. A session rewrites the tracked section back to the older text (today that drops the #6379 line and stamps `sha=0.129.12`). `agents:refresh` then treats the older text as current. A commit of that diff rolls the managed section back.

The recommended rule is the right rule for callers that plan with no template seam: `session:start` orientation, the `agents:refresh` command, and the host-surface drift probe. It is not enough to bind. The host hook writes the section earlier, through setup, and that call hands the runtime file in as the template. The recommended rule leaves that call alone, so a fresh worktree still receives the older section from the hook.

On the three questions. The plan function is the right place for the empty-seam callers, and it is not the only writer. Seams that already name this checkout can keep winning, and so can `DEFT_ROOT` when it is actually set to this checkout. ## In plain English
Problem: this repository's `AGENTS.md` managed section is generated from its own template, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. Sessions here run the pinned runtime, which carries an older copy of that template. A fresh worktree gets its section rewritten to the older text, and `agents:refresh` then calls the older text current. Workers restore the file again and again, and a commit that includes it rolls the rules back.

What the critic found: the recommended rule (read the checkout's own template in a source checkout) is right, but it missed the writer that acts first. Every hook call in a fresh worktree runs the setup step, and setup hands the runtime's own template to the refresh as an explicit input, so the rule never applied there. That is why the issue saw the runtime version stamped on the marker. The critic also showed that "the checkout's template" must mean the file `content/templates/agents-entry.md` itself: the general content resolver can prefer a staged content package over it.

Solution this lean proposes: two small changes. In a source checkout, a refresh that is given no template reads the checkout's file `content/templates/agents-entry.md` directly. And the setup step, in a source checkout, stops passing the runtime's template, so it takes that same path. A worktree whose `AGENTS.md` matches its own template is then left alone, and a template that is newer than `AGENTS.md` is reported as stale and written, as `agents:refresh` should do. Consumer projects are not source checkouts and keep exactly today's behavior.

What this adds: one condition in the plan function and one condition in the setup writer. No new gate, flag, refusal, grant or stored state.

What it does not do:
- It does not act before the next pin. The hook and the CLI run the pinned runtime's code, so the fix works in this repository once a release that carries it is pinned.
- It does not stop setup from writing other consumer files into this repository. That wider class is the operator-confirmed follow-up, not this story.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## In plain English

Problem: this repository's `AGENTS.md` managed section is generated from its own template, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`. Sessions here run the pinned runtime, which carries an older copy of that template. Every new worktree had its section rewritten to the older text, first by the setup step that each hook call runs and again by session start, and `agents:refresh` then called the older text current. A commit that included the file rolled the rules back.

Accepted solution: two small conditions. In a checkout of the framework source repository, a refresh that is given no template reads the checkout's own file `content/templates/agents-entry.md` and stamps the marker from the checkout. And the setup step, in a source checkout, stops passing the runtime's template, so it takes that same path. A worktree whose `AGENTS.md` matches its own template is left alone; a newer template is reported as stale and written. Consumer projects are not source checkouts and keep exactly today's refresh. Explicit seams and `DEFT_ROOT` keep winning.

Limits accepted: the fix acts in this repository once a release that carries it is pinned. Other consumer files that setup writes into this repository are a separate follow-up. The design adds no gate, flag, refusal, grant or stored state. It was checked by reading the source at the pinned commit; no code was run. No leftover next-build.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

In this repository (the framework source), the session hook rewrites the tracked `AGENTS.md` managed section from the pinned runtime's `templates/agents-entry.md` in every worktree where a session starts. Master's `AGENTS.md` is generated from the source template `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, which is often newer than the pinned runtime. So every new worktree gets an unasked, dirty `AGENTS.md` whose managed section is older than master's.

Workers must restore it again and again and keep it out of every commit. If one commits it, the PR silently rolls the managed section back.

This is the same class as the consumer `.gitattributes` deposit that #6337 fixed for this repository: a consumer-style deposit written into the framework repo's tracked files.

## Evidence (2026-11-17)

- 0.129.12 was cut at f082271e6. #6366 (bf05d3cd2) later added a rule to `content/templates/agents-entry.md` and master's `AGENTS.md`: "Run `swarm:pre-dispatch` (begin) before any implementation worker ... (#6379)".
- In a fresh worktree from origin/master (139fdc3bb) with runtime 0.129.12, the managed section was rewritten (marker `sha=0.129.12`). The diff removes that #6379 line and brings back older wording in four other places (the #3124 mirror note, "#4383 closed", the #5732 leftover note).
- `deft agents:refresh` then reported "unchanged - sha match", so it treats the rolled-back section as current.
- The #6480 worker reported the session hook rewrote AGENTS.md repeatedly in its worktree; it restored the file each time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a session starts in a worktree of the framework source repository, then the hook does not rewrite the tracked `AGENTS.md` managed section from the pinned runtime.
- Given the pinned runtime's template is older than the repository's source template, then `agents:refresh` does not report the older section as current.
- Consumer projects keep today's managed-section refresh.

## Notes

- Related: #6337 (same class for `.gitattributes`), #1309 (template propagation).
- Until fixed, the drift clears when a release that carries the newer template is pinned.
